lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: data and uncertainty

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: A model predicts a $80 rate will increase by 25%. What is the new rate?

steps: Identify what the problem is asking and which quantities, assumptions, or constraints matter.
Build and solve a model, then check the result against the context.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: A storage container is designed as a rectangular prism 3 ft long, 9 ft wide, and 4 ft high. What is its volume in cubic feet?
A data set has the values 5, 20, 35, 50, 65. The mean is 35. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD), a measure of the data's uncertainty or spread?
A student claims a box that is 4 by 5 by 6 units has a volume of 15 cubic units. Evaluate the claim.
choices: Yes; the volume is 15 cubic units.
Cannot be determined from the given information.
No; the volume is 17 cubic units, not 15.
No; the volume is 120 cubic units, not 15.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: A rental company charges a $8 base fee plus $5 per hour. A customer's total bill was $53. Which equation models this situation, and how many hours were rented?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A diver starts at the surface (0 m) and descends 7 m, then descends another 24 m, then ascends 12 m. The dive plan assumes a depth limit of 42 m below the surface. What is the diver's final position, as a signed number of meters?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A model predicts a $280 rate will decrease by 10%. What does the model predict as the new rate?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
